posts.title: What you need to install a dimmer switch (and when to call an electrician)
posts.summary: The parts and checks for swapping a standard light switch for a dimmer, including the compatibility trap that makes lamps buzz.
intro: A dimmer swap is one of the simplest electrical jobs there is: isolate the circuit, change the switch, put it back. It is also one of the easiest to get wrong, because the dimmer and the lamps have to be compatible.

Before anything else: in many places this is notifiable work, or must be done by a qualified electrician. Check your local rules. Nothing here is a substitute for isolating the circuit properly and testing that it is dead.
list: Dimmer switch, matched to your lamp type
LED, halogen and incandescent need different dimmers — buy for the lamps you actually have
Prove the circuit is dead before you touch it. This is not optional
Insulated handles; a live conductor can still be present in a two-way circuit
Old switch wires are often nicked and need trimming back
If the existing wires are too short to reach the new terminals
Match the finish and the fixings to the dimmer

tiers.label: Cheapest that works
tiers.text: A basic trailing-edge dimmer and a standard faceplate. Fine for a single incandescent or a matched dimmable LED.

tiers.label: Buy the good one
tiers.text: A trailing-edge dimmer rated for the total LED load on the circuit, with a proper metal faceplate. Cheap leading-edge dimmers are the ones that buzz and flicker with LED lamps.

skip.what: A dimmer rated for the wrong load
skip.why: Dimmers have a minimum and maximum load. Fifteen low-wattage LED lamps can sit below the minimum, so the dimmer flickers or drops out entirely. Add up the actual wattage on the circuit before choosing.
It is not a dimmer fault. Non-dimmable drivers buzz, flicker or fail early. Check the lamp packaging says dimmable before assuming the switch is broken.

skip.what: Working on a circuit you have not proved dead
skip.why: Switching the breaker off is not proof. Test at the terminals with a known-good tester. In a two-way circuit another conductor can still be live.

maths: Add up the load before buying: eight 6 W LED lamps is 48 W total. A dimmer with a 5 W minimum and a 100 W LED maximum sits comfortably; one with a 20 W minimum would not.
Check box depth, not just the switch: a deeper dimmer body may not fit a shallow back box, which is the most common reason a swap stalls halfway.
posts.outro: If the wiring is aluminium, the box is full of unknown joints, or your local rules require a certificate, use a qualified electrician. This is the one page on this site where doing it yourself has a legal edge as well as a safety one.

posts.title: What you need to hang a heavy mirror on drywall
posts.summary: The complete list for hanging a mirror over 10 kg on plasterboard, and why the fixing matters more than the hook.
intro: A heavy mirror is a static load with a lever arm. That combination is what pulls fixings out of drywall: the weight is not the problem, the weight times the distance from the wall is.
The list below assumes a mirror of roughly 10-15 kg on plasterboard, with the option of a stud if one happens to be under the hang point.
list: Rated well above the mirror weight; spreads load behind the board
Mirror clips or a French cleat
A cleat spreads the load across the mirror back instead of two points
Stops the mirror rattling against the wall and protects the plaster
Mirrors are the least forgiving thing to hang out of level
If you can hit a stud, do — no anchor needed
Mark the line, and tape the mirror edge as a drilling guide

tiers.label: Cheapest that works
tiers.text: A basic toggle anchor set and a simple hook. Only if the mirror sits close to the wall and is under about 10 kg.

tiers.label: Buy the good one
tiers.text: Toggle anchors plus a French cleat. The cleat converts two point loads into a distributed one across the back of the mirror — the single change that makes a heavy mirror safe.

skip.what: Picture wire on a heavy mirror
skip.why: Wire reduces the rated capacity of a fixing dramatically and lets the mirror shift. A cleat or direct-fixed clips are the right answer above a few kilos.
Same failure as with shelves: they grip the paper face, not the board. A 15 kg mirror is well outside what they hold.

skip.what: Hanging on a stud only if it lands off-centre
skip.why: Hitting a stud 200 mm off-centre to save an anchor is a bad trade. Use a proper anchor and hang the mirror where it belongs.

maths: Two toggle anchors rated at 25 kg each give a nominal 50 kg capacity for a 15 kg mirror — a safety factor of well over three. That margin matters because drywall strength varies and the load is applied through a lever.
Use the widest horizontal spacing the mirror back allows. Doubling the spacing halves the pull-out force on each fixing.
posts.outro: If the wall is lath and plaster rather than modern plasterboard, treat it as a different material entirely — it crumbles around a fixing and needs a different anchor.

posts.title: What you need to seal a leaking shower (and how to find the actual leak)
posts.summary: The list for re-sealing a shower tray and enclosure, plus the order of work that stops you sealing the wrong joint.
intro: Most shower leaks that look like tray leaks are actually a failed joint higher up, or a blocked drain channel pushing water sideways. Seal the wrong thing and the leak comes back in a fortnight.
The list below covers the honest case: cutting out old sealant, drying properly, and re-sealing the joints that move.
list: Fungicidal and flexible. Standard sealant grows mould in a wet area
Silicone remover or a sealant removal tool
Cutting out the old bead completely is most of the job
A consistent bead seals; a smeared one does not
Surfaces must be clean and dry or sealant will not bond
Cracked grout in the enclosure is often the real leak path
A partially blocked drain channel lets water pool and find a way out

tiers.label: Cheapest that works
tiers.text: Own-brand sanitary sealant and a basic smoothing tool. Acceptable for a rental repair you expect to redo.

tiers.label: Buy the good one
tiers.text: A high-movement sealant designed for joints that move, plus a profiling kit. Shower tray joints move; a rigid sealant cracks.

skip.why: New sealant will not bond to old cured silicone. It looks fine for a week and then peels. Cut the old bead out completely — it is most of the job for a reason.

skip.what: Sealing a joint that is still damp
skip.why: Silicone will not adhere to a wet surface. After cutting out, leave the joint to dry fully, and if the wall behind is soaked, stop and find the actual leak first.

skip.what: Using grout where the joint needs to move
skip.why: Corners and tray joints move with temperature and weight. Grout cracks there; flexible sealant does not. That is what the gap is for.

maths: Silicone coverage: a standard tube lays roughly 10-12 m of a 6 mm bead. The perimeter of a typical 900 × 900 mm shower tray is 3.6 m plus the enclosure uprights, so one tube usually covers it and the second is your margin for a re-run.
Curing: most sanitary sealants need around 24 hours before the shower is used. Plan the job for a day when nobody needs the shower.
posts.outro: If the ceiling below the bathroom is stained, the leak is likely from the waste or the supply rather than the sealant. Sealing will not fix that.

posts.title: What you need to build a simple workbench that stays rigid
posts.summary: Timber, fixings and the diagonal that stops a workbench racking — sized for a 1800 x 600 mm bench.
intro: A workbench fails in one specific way: it racks. Push it sideways and the whole frame turns into a parallelogram, because there is nothing resisting the movement.
The fix is cheap — a diagonal brace or a back panel — and the rest of the list is just timber and screws.
list: Legs, rails and aprons; standard length suits an 1800 mm bench
A solid core door or a glued-up timber top; avoid chipboard for a work surface
Exterior wood screws, 100 mm and 65 mm
Long screws for the frame, shorter for the top and braces
Bolted joints stay tight through vibration where screws work loose
Plywood back panel or diagonal brace
This is what stops the racking. Do not leave it out
Glue plus screws is much stronger than screws alone
Almost no floor is flat; the bench should not rock

tiers.label: Cheapest that works
tiers.text: Standard structural timber and a plywood top. It will be rigid if you brace it, and it will mark easily — accept that.

tiers.label: Buy the good one
tiers.text: A thicker bench top and bolted joints with a plywood back panel. A heavier top is what makes a bench pleasant to work on: it absorbs hammer blows instead of ringing.

skip.what: Skipping the back panel or diagonal brace
skip.why: This is the single decision that determines whether the bench is usable. Four legs and a top with square joints racks immediately under sideways load.

skip.what: A chipboard or MDF top for a workbench
skip.why: It swells and crumbles the first time it gets wet or takes a hammer blow. Plywood or solid timber is not much more expensive and lasts far longer.

skip.what: Nailing the frame instead of screwing and gluing it
skip.why: Nails pull out under vibration. Screws with glue, or bolts at the leg joints, are what keep a bench tight for years.

maths: Timber: four legs at 900 mm and four rails totalling 4.8 m for an 1800 mm bench comes to about 8.4 m of timber. At 2400 mm per length, that is 4 lengths, plus 2 for the aprons and the brace — 6 in total.

Bench height: most people are comfortable with a bench top around wrist height when standing, commonly 850-900 mm. Measure rather than copying a number — a bench at the wrong height is a bench you avoid using.
posts.outro: Cut and drill in a ventilated space, and check for nails or screws before cutting any reclaimed timber.

posts.title: What you need to lay a laminate floor over a weekend
posts.summary: Underlay, spacers and the expansion gap: the complete list for a 20 m² laminate floor, including the part people skip.
intro: Laminate is a floating floor: it is not fixed down, and it expands. Almost every laminate failure is either an uneven subfloor or a missing expansion gap.
This list is sized for a 20 m² room and assumes you are laying over an existing hard floor rather than removing it.
list: Packs state coverage, typically around 2.2 m²; add 10% for waste
Smooths minor unevenness and reduces noise
Keeps the gap at every wall while you lay
Only over a concrete or solid floor — essential there
Covers the expansion gap at the wall
Bridges the gap between rooms and allows movement
Only if the subfloor is out by more than the tolerance on the pack

tiers.label: Cheapest that works
tiers.text: Thin foam underlay and a basic laminate. Honest for a low-traffic spare room; it will sound hollow and feel thin underfoot.

tiers.label: Buy the good one
tiers.text: A thicker acoustic underlay and a laminate with a decent wear layer. The underlay is what removes the hollow click and takes up small subfloor imperfections, so it does more for how the floor feels than the board does.

skip.what: Leaving no expansion gap at the walls
skip.why: The floor grows with humidity. Without a gap it lifts at the middle or buckles at a doorway. The gap is not cosmetic — the skirting hides it.

skip.what: Laying over an uneven concrete floor without checking
skip.why: Laminate flexes over humps and the joints fail. Check flatness with a long straight edge; the pack states the tolerance. Levelling compound is much cheaper than replacing a floor.

skip.what: Laying laminate in a bathroom or a wet room
skip.why: Even water-resistant laminate has a core that swells at the edges. For a bathroom, use a product actually rated for wet areas, or a different floor entirely.

maths: Packs: a 20 m² room plus 10% waste is 22 m². At roughly 2.2 m² per pack that is 10 packs. Buy at least one spare pack and keep it — a discontinued board is almost impossible to match later.
Perimeter gap: allow about 10 mm at every wall for a 20 m² room, which is what the spacers are for. That is why skirting or scotia is on the list rather than optional.
posts.outro: Acclimatise the packs flat in the room for about 48 hours before laying. Boards laid straight from a cold store can shrink after installation and open up at the joints.
